title: Prismriver, explained
h1: Music theory in Lean: pitches, intervals and the dihedral group of triads
lead: Prismriver is mostly a music library (a note-entry DSL, scores, MusicXML and Alda output, algorithmic composition). Its proved core is small and clean: intervals act on spelled pitches like an abelian group acting on a space, and every pitch-level transposition or inversion lands exactly on the matching element of the 12-element-rotation dihedral group acting on (pitch class, major/minor) pairs.
desc: An unofficial plain-English guide to Prismriver, Leni Aniva and Claire Wang's Lean 4 library for music theory and algorithmic composition: what its theorems about intervals, transposition and the dihedral group D12 actually say.
startNote: Prismriver is a music library first and a theorem library second. Start with Interval and Pitch (how a note is spelled), then the Torsor instance (intervals really act on pitches). The headline is transposeAction_toDihedral_triad: transposing or inverting a pitch matches the D12 action on pitch classes.
sizeNote: About 3,600 lines of Lean in 23 files under Prismriver/; roughly 50 theorems, nearly all in four files.
agentCtx: Prismriver: a Lean 4 music-theory and algorithmic-composition library (pitches, intervals, scales, scores, LilyPond-like DSL, MusicXML/Alda IO) with proofs that intervals act on pitches and that transposition/inversion is compatible with the dihedral group D12.

gloss.DihedralGroup: Mathlib's DihedralGroup n: the symmetries of a regular n-gon, with n rotations r i and n reflections sr i (indices in ZMod n). Here n = 12, the clock of pitch classes.
gloss.DihedralGroup.r: A rotation r i of the 12-gon; musically, transposition by i semitones.
gloss.DihedralGroup.sr: A reflection sr i of the 12-gon; musically, an inversion (mirror) of pitch classes.
gloss.ZMod: ZMod 12: the integers modulo 12, i.e. the twelve pitch classes C, C♯, …, B with clock arithmetic.
gloss.MulAction: A group action: a way for each group element g to move points x to g • x, with 1 • x = x and (g·h) • x = g • (h • x).
gloss.Equivalence: Lean core's Equivalence r: r is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
